entries.note: REAL - measured: diff=1 requests 4e7 Hz; only a low clamp exists (timer.c:82-83,139-140).

REAL - source-verified. Nuance: the HOST burst needs only emulated_hz>0, so default pmax permits it; only the guest interrupt storm needs non-EXC3K.
REAL - source-verified. vocore is the worst default: 3.6e8 Hz -> ~5.5M iterations per signal. Resync widens, never bounds, the burst.
REAL - reading. Counter-nuance: R3000 guests do not write Compare (no such register), so default pmax boots do not reach even the host burst. Any cap is arbitrary - the model is the defect.
REAL - reading. Adds: SA_RESTART without SA_NODEFER; no INTERRUPT_DEASSERT of IP7 in cpus/; algor 1.67e8 Hz is the worst live default; interval 0 (1/inf) never advances.
REAL - packet.
REAL - packet.
REAL - packet.

REAL - the missing clamp is real AND the symptom of a deeper modeling error: a ONE-SHOT deadline delta is converted into a PERIODIC frequency. Clamp = blast-radius control; the deadline-as-frequency model is a design item to FILE, not to fix in this batch.

ONE helper clamps into [1e-8, 32768], stores only after the clamp, snaps a 1024-iteration catch-up, and sanitises the rtc value. The lowest bound proposed.
packet: clamp to [1e-8, 1e7] at entry to both functions; guard interval INDEPENDENTLY of freq.
packet: a FINITE 10 MHz upper bound; guard interval after the division; bound the catch-up with a resync; store the clamped value.
packet: clamp to an IN-TREE-JUSTIFIED bound (declining to invent a number without the callers) and fix the :137 pre-clamp store.

REFRAMED THE ROUND: the panel's 300:1 spread on the ceiling is itself evidence that A FIXED CEILING IS THE WRONG INSTRUMENT - the measured harm is iterations per signal, and even the largest proposed ceiling leaves ~153,846 of them. The catch-up CAP is the protection; the ceiling is domain normalisation. Also: the report belongs at the CLAMP SITE (device context, where fatal() is already idiom), not in the handler - and the SIGALRM hazard codex worried about does not exist there. NaN is caught by NEGATING the comparisons that must exist anyway, at zero marginal cost: A FREE GUARD AT A TRUST BOUNDARY NEEDS NO REACHABILITY PROOF. Committed against shipping the loop bound alone, because interval=0 would then burn the cap every signal for ever.

MEASURED EVERYTHING, AND OVERTURNED TWO PROPOSALS. Built the offline driver and proved timer.c CAN be driven in the diff_*.c idiom (one stub: gettimeofday). CENSUS: emulated_hz is an int, so INT_MAX bounds every legitimate request - the ceiling is DERIVED, not picked. POLICY TABLE: 'drop missed ticks' is NOT A POLICY BUT A DEFECT (it caps every timer at 65 Hz - a 100 Hz timer runs at rate 0.65 with no burst at all); the flagship's cap of 65536 BREAKS a legitimate 4e7 Hz timer (1.0000 -> 0.1065); 2^20 is the smallest power of two that leaves every legitimate case BIT-IDENTICAL to shipped. And clamping at :137 alone is not just insufficient but A REGRESSION - it loses idempotence on five of six classes because the early-out then compares a clamped record against a raw request. Caught its own first probe (it held time fixed and would have cleared the defect).

SHIP-WITH-FIX. Two findings nobody else had in full: the cap and the domain are INCONSISTENT (the domain admits INT_MAX but cap x base can only ever serve 68,157,440 ticks/s, so above that the debt grows forever and 'delivered by the signals that follow' is untrue), and it is REACHABLE through cpu_mips_coproc at compare_diff==1: 166.56 MHz on Algor, 360 MHz on VoCore. So R4's 'every legitimate case bit-identical' is FALSE. Also found the gate floor at 13 vs 14 rows, the constant-deletion mutant, and interval=0.5/freq sailing over every floor. Sandbox denied execution, so MANUAL not CONFIRMED, and it said so.

SHIP-WITH-FIX, and the only seat that COMPILED AND RAN. MEASURED six mutants that break a claimed property and pass all seven of gate 2's diff_timer checks. Then found a LIVE HOST CRASH the round had not looked for: dev_footbridge.c:141 does random() %% a guest-written zero -- reproduced as SIGFPE, core dumped -- and #427/#428 CONVERT THE OLD HANG INTO IT. Also measured the four-timer cost at 69%% of a host period (inside the band the header's own reasoning rejects), the complaint flood at 1000-for-1000, and traced dev_sh4's exit(1) from inside SIGALRM. Verified afterwards that it had mutated only its own copies.

SHIP-WITH-FIX. Caught an error in MY BRIEF while still streaming -- 'the header says 65 Hz, not the brief's 100 Hz' -- which was right, and the brief's own 0.65 figure gave it away. Independently found the gate floor at 13 and the constant-immune bound row, and named the discriminating case for deduct-vs-drop. Its caller table is the most complete of the reading seats. Shell and git were denied, so it read rather than ran, and said so in the verdict.

SHIP-WITH-FIX, and it EXECUTED: three mutants CONFIRMED by running them, including the one that matters most for coverage -- reverting #429 entirely leaves gate 2 fully green, because nothing under regress/ compiles dev_rtc.c. Also MEASURED that stall=0.0 and stall=100000.0 give byte-identical output, and did the twelve-caller audit the packet seats had to mark UNKNOWN. Mutated copies only; the live trees were verified clean afterwards.

SHIP-WITH-FIX. Named deleting timer_catchup_hit=1 as the smallest edit that breaks a claimed property and passes everything, and caught that the 'still delivers what it could' row (n>0) cannot tell retention from dropping. Went row by row against the defect each row names. Used 65 Hz correctly throughout despite the brief's error, because the packet inlines the header.

HOLD -- the strongest dissent, and it was right on both counts. (1) The budget is PER TIMER and the header's derivation assumes ONE, so N timers cost N x 2^20 in a signal. (2) The stall is INERT: timer_current_time is advanced by the handler and the gettimeofday stub is never called because fresh() disabled the resync -- traced without running anything. Also showed the round's 'schedule is already ahead' explanation is arithmetically false.

SHIP-WITH-FIX, 9.5 KB -- its third consecutive real answer under the packet convention. Reached the same false-negative conclusion independently and gave the recipe for the discriminating row (owed > cap on one signal, < cap on the next). Uniquely named a property NO ROW CAN EVER CATCH here -- volatile sig_atomic_t -> int passes because no signal handler is installed -- and said the round should RECORD that rather than imply coverage. It also stated the test that would settle its own finding if it were wrong.

DELIBERATELY NOT FIRED, and this is a deferral rather than a seat failure or agreement. The owner warned of the hourly Fable limit; the seat is reserved for tonight's batched regression review, where P11 makes it the only required seat. Recorded by name so a later reader cannot mistake an unfired seat for a silent one.

*** ANSWERED 192 KB AND WAS NEVER RECORDED UNTIL THE OWNER SPOTTED THE BLANK CELL (2026-08-16). *** It was not a seat failure and not a quota wall -- kimi was answering 66-192 KB in every panel that week. The review simply never reached the ledger, which is the same unread-seat defect this project caught a day earlier, one layer out. VERDICT: SHIP-WITH-FIX -- the emulator code is correct as committed; the DETECTOR has holes. ITS BIGGEST FINDING, VERIFIED: **gate 2 has ZERO coverage of dev_rtc.c** -- no compile check, no behaviour row, not even a grep (`grep -c rtc regress/gate_offline.sh` returns 0, and the only mention of dev_rtc anywhere in regress/ is a comment inside diff_timer.c). So #429's range-check fix at dev_rtc.c:131-135 is ENTIRELY UNGATED OFFLINE: reverting it leaves gate 2 green. REGRESS_PASS, 16/16, 0 failed, 0 SKIPPED, 1,043 ok rows -- and the arithmetic was verified: 1,043 is exactly the sum of the sixteen per-gate counts, so no phantom rows. The chain that lets offline rows speak for rig binaries is CLOSED: the diffs compile SEC repo source, gate 1 proves both build trees byte-synced to SEC, the rigs run the build binaries. THE VERDICT IS DELIBERATELY DEFLATIONARY: this green licenses 'every R1-R9 detector still passes against today's source, and four rigs still boot'. It does NOT license 'every R1-R9 fix is still present' -- #429 and #431 are both revertible under a green battery -- and it does NOT license 'the new detectors can still fail', because gate 3 is the only failability control and all seven of its mutants target float_emul.c, none of the five harnesses R4-R9 added. COI disclosed by the seat itself: the R1-R9 commits carry its own Co-Authored-By, so this is same-model review of same-model work (A,s), and it weighted construction-proofs over judgement accordingly.  ROUND-SPECIFIC: Same split as tfreq: the timer half is well covered, the dev_rtc half is not. CONFIRMED.

PASS 1 MEASURE SEAT -- built a private tree, BOOTED THE RIG, and refuted three of my own measurements.
* REACHABILITY, MEASURED POSITIVE, so this is a FIX not a document: instrumented the SCSI dispatch and booted luna88k UNMODIFIED to login:. The guest issues SYNCHRONIZE CACHE (0x35) ONCE, immediately after the log line '/dev/sd0a: MARKING FILE SYSTEM CLEAN' -- the exact moment the command exists for, and the worst moment to lose a write tail. pmax runs OpenBSD 2.2 whose scsi/ contains no 0x35 at all; landisk is ATA, not SCSI.
* THE DETECTOR IT BUILT AND THEN ATTACKED: 34 rows, 17 fail on shipping code, 0 with the fix, identical at -O0 and -O2, 0 faults. THREE OF ITS FOUR ATTACKS DEFEATED IT: nblk 4->16 (ONE DIGIT -- one whole buffer flushes completely), exit() instead of _exit(), and the one my brief did not list -- ONE MORE SCSI READ AFTER THE SYNC, whose my_fseek flushes the pending write. Any realistic-looking test that does anything at all after the sync is silently green.
* THE VACUITY CLASS THAT WOULD HAVE SUNK THE ROUND: run the same binary with its workdir on /mnt/c (drvfs, st_blksize=512 -- where _scratchpad, _images and BOTH RIGS live) and EVERY byte row passes with the defect fully present, because each 512-byte fwrite reaches the kernel immediately. Its [VACUITY CONTROL] row fires and declares the section meaningless. The --wrap=fsync/fflush call-recording rows stay red on drvfs -- filesystem-independent, and the ONLY rows that can see defect (b) at all.
* Q1 NO do_fsync GATE, with costs: dirty fflush+fsync 5.85 ms ext4, clean 0.56 ms. The flood surface ALREADY SHIPS (the handler fsyncs unconditionally today); the fix makes it at most ~3x, synchronous and single-threaded, so a guest cannot get asynchronous amplification. Not the cflood shape -- there the cost is a diagnostic, here the cost IS the semantics.
* Q2 YES, same class as #286, and #416/#417 already settled the harder half: :907-910 already returns MEDIUM ERROR for HOST-side failures, and #417 tested it against a real errno (RLIMIT_FSIZE -> EFBIG). Honest UNKNOWN: Linux >=4.13 reports an fsync failure ONCE and drops the dirty pages, so a LATER sync returns success after data was already lost.
* Q3 DO NOT sync d->f under overlays, and it is worse than pointless: diskimage.c:1984 opens d->f in mode r whenever prefix_R is set while :1971 sets writable=1, so R: -- WHAT BOTH RIGS USE -- gives a writable disk whose base handle is READ-ONLY, and the temp overlay is already unlinked. fflush on a read-mode stream is UB in C99 7.21.5.2p2; fsync on O_RDONLY is rc=0 on glibc but UNKNOWN on NetBSD/OpenBSD/Solaris, where it would turn every R:/CD-ROM sync into a spurious MEDIUM ERROR. Plus 14.34 ms to fsync a 512 MB untouched file on drvfs.
* Q5 ONE COMMAND: luna88k issued START STOP UNIT 5x, ALL with cmd[4]=0x01 (START, no LOEJ, no STOP). The durability-adjacent case was never observed.
* ADVERSARIAL -- THREE DEFECTS IN MY PROPOSED FUNCTION, one measured into silent corruption: (i) int ok = 1 returns SUCCESS for a disk with nothing open, losing the #134 diagnostic; (ii) THE ORDERING HOLE -- it sets ok=0 on a failed overlay-data fsync AND THEN FSYNCS THE BITMAP ANYWAY, publishing 'the overlay owns block N' while N's bytes are not durable. It BUILT that state and drove the shipping read path: the guest reads 0x00 from the overlay's HOLE and the base's good 0xBB bytes are GONE -- silent corruption of data the guest never touched, reported as a successful read. It does NOT fall through to the base. Honest counterweight: NOT reproducible in the current write path (BIT_SET_BUT_DATA_MISSING=0 across n=1..129; the per-block fseeks keep them in lockstep), so it is a hole the FIX would INTRODUCE, not a live defect; (iii) directory-entry durability CHECKED AND NOT A HOLE -- user overlays open r+ and must pre-exist, and the only created file is the unlinked temp overlay. An honest negative.
* Also found: there is NO fclose of d->f or the overlays at shutdown anywhere. A clean exit() flushes stdio so a normal quit is safe, but a SIGKILLed emulator loses the tail regardless.
* ITS OWN ERROR, reported rather than dropped: its first detector left c.nblk UNINITIALIZED, so every overlay row went red -- AGREEING WITH ITS HYPOTHESIS -- and at -O2 malloc(512*garbage) SIGSEGVd into 4 FAULTS it nearly reported as an overlay-path defect. Its own words: a red row that confirms your hypothesis is the dangerous kind.  [panel_20260817_215052]

*** NAMED A MEASUREMENT NOBODY HAD RUN AND TOLD ME TO RUN IT BEFORE WRITING THE CHANGELOG SENTENCE: an fflush-ONLY (no fsync) arm. Its words: 'If that arm persists after _exit, the kill-and-check row is not an fsync test.' I RAN IT AND IT WAS RIGHT. *** MEASURED, one 512-byte write: fflush only -> 512 bytes DURABLE to a separate reader; fsync only (what ships today) -> 0. So _exit() simulates PROCESS death, not host death -- the page cache belongs to the KERNEL and outlives the process -- and a kill-and-check test therefore measures the missing FFLUSH, never the missing FSYNC. This SPLITS THE DEFECT: (a) missing fflush is byte-testable and bounded; (b) overlays never fsynced at all is NOT byte-testable by ANY process-kill test, needs the --wrap rows, and is unbounded on real power loss. It also placed the detector correctly (beside diff_diskimage_io.c, NOT on the #411 write-fail fixtures) and filed six things explicitly NOT to do this round.  [panel_20260817_215052]
GO-WITH-CHANGES. diskimage_sync() with fflush+fsync covering overlays and base, propagate CHECK CONDITION on sync failure, and keep scope bounded to SYNCHRONIZE CACHE.  [panel_20260817_215052]

And the row NAMES overclaimed -- 'fflushes data and bitmap' passed with the bitmap untouched, and the gate grepped those exact names as its evidence.
* *** AND THE FIXTURE HAD NEVER WRITTEN A BYTE. *** SCSICMD_WRITE is 0x0a = WRITE(6) driven with a 10-byte CDB, so the length parsed as 256 blocks; and the handler requires data_out_offset == size, which the fixture never set. Both overlay files were 0 bytes after every run -- corroborated by identical 0-byte leftovers already in the repo from an earlier run. THAT is why the file-blind mutants lived: with nothing written there is no durability property to check, only call counts.
* Q1 THE `continue` IS RIGHT -- it tried and could not build a state where skipping is worse; a stale bitmap makes a read fall through to the base (stale but real) rather than to the overlay's hole (zeros). TWO CORRECTIONS AROUND IT: the comment overclaims, because after 4 writes with NO sync an independent reader already sees bitmap[0]=0x07 -- the per-block fseeks already pushed both to the page cache, so the continue declines to FORCE publication rather than preventing it; and a multi-overlay disk reports CHECK CONDITION when a non-last overlay's fsync fails even though every guest byte is durable.

rows.title: gateflr  If a whole gate block is deleted, nothing outside it notices
rows.hold: FILE: measured during the R1+R2 regression review

closure.note: Found by the flagship while reviewing the R1 and R2 regression evidence. The new gate-2 block guards itself: its floors, its named-row greps and its positive control are all INSIDE the block. Delete the block and every one of those guards disappears with it, while the gate still reports PASS - nothing outside floors gate 2's check count. This is the vacuity class in a new place: not a row that cannot fail, but a whole section that can be removed silently. A committed per-gate check-count floor, asserted by the runner rather than by the gate, is the shape of the fix.

rows.title: hlen  Device handlers that ignore the access length (audit)
rows.hold: census done; promote to a FIX round?

closure.note: Opened from the b75 refutation, then characterized by census. A device handler that switches on the address and cannot service a width will read or write only the first register of an 8-byte access. MEASURED SCOPE: 62 spanning-capable handlers of 167 registered; 20 on machines this project boots. TWO BOOTED MACHINES ARE PROVABLY IMMUNE - SH-4 has no 8-byte access at all (fmov.d is two 4-byte accesses) and MIPS32/R3000A treats LD/SD as reserved, so landisk and pmax cannot produce the access. NO CONVENTION EXISTS in the tree: no helper, no macro, no rule - only three hand-rolled decompositions that are all big-endian-specific and that disagree with each other about the else branch, so there is no single idiom to copy. FIRST WITNESS NAMED: dev_irqc on testarm, the only spanning-capable device on that machine, where the two halves of one aligned 8-byte access have OPPOSITE legal directions (status is read-only, mask is write-only), which makes the miss unambiguous. DETECTOR SHAPE: an offline differential in the diff_*.c family - no boot, no rig, no serialization.

entries.note: CENSUS: 118 files, 62 spanning-capable handlers, 20 on booted machines. Coverage PROVED by set-difference against the 167 registered handlers, not asserted. THE DISCRIMINATOR IS NOT WHETHER len IS MENTIONED: 115 of 167 pass len only to memory_readmax64, which marshals bytes and does nothing about a span across two registers - so 'uses len' does not mean safe, and the naive definition undercounts the class about 15 times. Also measured: fatal() DOES NOT HALT (debugmsg.c:384 is a plain wrapper), so the 8 warn-then-service handlers are the defect with a log line.

rows.hold: FILE - independent of the b47 fix

closure.note: The fast path masks the effective address while the slow path uses the raw address, so one instruction has two behaviours. Round #357 made unaligned bases persist, which makes this more reachable than before. Sites source-verified by the measure seat.

entries.note: *** TRUE, AND ITS 'ZERO SEAT ENTRIES' IS A LEDGER ARTIFACT, NOT AN UNASSESSED ITEM. *** OUTSTANDING_BUGS.md:2698+ ALREADY HOLDS THE FULL ANALYSIS -- verified independently by the main loop, which found the existing text naming the same mechanism. Re-verified the mechanism anyway: cpu_arm_instr.c:1550 fast path does p32[(addr & 0xfff) >> 2] (the >>2 truncates addr[1:0], which IS the architectural answer) while :1563 slow path hands raw addr to memory_rw -- same instruction, two answers, selected by PAGE RESIDENCY. Thumb PUSH/POP inherits it (cpu_arm.c:1670,1677). AND IT RE-CHECKED THE ARM CITATIONS AGAINST THE REAL LOCAL MANUAL, all three holding: LDM(1) p.A4-37, STM(1) p.A4-190, Table A2-10 'Operation unaffected by Addr[1:0]' p.A2-40 -- its own first grep reported them unverifiable and that was ITS error, caught by re-grepping. *** REPRODUCED, AND THE FIX IS MEASURED RATHER THAN ARGUED. *** Probe built on the testarm/SA1110 cold debugger with a four-byte raw stub; every encoding re-verified through the emulator's own unassemble before any row was believed. Three binaries in a private tree:
* HEAD scores 9/15 rows against the architecture; MASK AT THE ACCESS scores 15/15; MASK AT ENTRY scores 14/15 and CORRUPTS THE BASE WRITEBACK (0x00070004 for 0x00070006). *** #357's 'mask at entry corrupts the writeback' is REAL, NOT FOLKLORE -- the mutant was built and measured. ***
* The divergence, three ways: the SAME LDM run twice against one page returns 0x77881122 then 0x11223344; ONE LDM WITH TWO REGISTERS returns r1 from a raw unaligned address and r3 from an aligned one -- MIXED WITHIN A SINGLE INSTRUCTION, because r1's own access warmed the page; and a cold STM SPILLS INTO THE NEXT WORD (0x00FF3344 / 0x5566FFFF).
* IT SIDESTEPPED THE `put w` WARMS / `put b` DOES NOT TRAP RATHER THAN TRUSTING IT: the slow path's own memory_rw inserts the page on its way out (memory_rw.c:732, no NO_EXCEPTIONS), so the first bdt access to a cold page is slow and every later one is fast. Running the IDENTICAL instruction twice makes the divergence a difference between two executions rather than a value that depends on trusting a seeding rule.
* FIX: two lines, cpu_arm_instr.c:1563 (load) and :1752 (store), addr -> addr & ~(uint32_t)3. Confirmed from the CODE (`uint32_t addr = *np` at :1514, `if (w_bit) *np = addr` at :1624 -- addr IS the writeback value), from the LOCAL manual (A5.4.2 p.A5-43; LDM(1) p.A4-37, STM(1) p.A4-190), and from the ENTRY mutant. NUANCE it caught: the Multi-word row of Table A2-10 is on the CONTINUATION page A2-41, not A2-40 where the table starts.
* IN-TREE PRECEDENT it did not expect: generate_arm_multi.c:117 already emits `addr &= 0xffc` and the generated combiners write back from the UNMASKED register -- upstream's own generated LDM combiners already use exactly this shape, and they fall back to instr(bdt_load) on a cold page, so they inherit both the defect and the fix. Thumb PUSH/POP (cpu_arm.c:1670,1677) call the same two functions; arm_pop/arm_push have exactly four callers, all enumerated.
* *** THE EXISTING GATE IS BLIND TO IT, MEASURED: arm_writeback_probe.py scores 22/22 on ALL THREE binaries including the ENTRY mutant that corrupts the writeback, and gate 14's 261 checks touch neither arm_pop nor arm_push. *** The single check separating the correct fix from the #357 trap is the W=1 writeback row. So the gate row is NOT redundant and must land in the SAME commit as the fix, being scored against architecture rather than against HEAD.
* Side effect named rather than left to be found: masking also removes the 4 KB page-straddle path for bdt, where a raw access at P+0xFFE currently translates once and takes its tail from the physical continuation.
* It also caught a records defect against the main loop: _scratchpad/CHECKPOINT.md had gone stale, naming HEAD 4d0981d and 'Tree CLEAN' when HEAD was 9bcae1c and two files were uncommitted. Re-derived.  [agent armbdt 2026-08-19]

rows.title: capgap  The timer domain admits 32x more than the catch-up cap can ever serve
rows.hold: design question, not a defect; needs a policy decision

entries.note: Two seats, independently. The domain admits INT_MAX Hz; the cap delivers at most TIMER_MAX_CATCHUP * TIMER_BASE_FREQUENCY = 68,157,440 ticks/s. Between them the debt grows without bound -- MEASURED at 0.9683 s behind after one simulated second, delivered ratio 0.0317. Reached via cpu_mips_coproc at compare_diff==1 (166.56 MHz Algor, 360 MHz VoCore), so R4's 'every legitimate case bit-identical' is FALSE for those machines. NOT made worse by R4 (the old code spun 33 million iterations per signal at the same rate). The question is whether an unserviceable rate should be rejected, dropped, or left to lag -- a policy decision, which is why it is filed rather than fixed.

rows.title: constblind  Every differential that reads a #define for its expected value is blind to that #define
rows.hold: AUDITED: diff_timer was the only one exposed; now fixed

entries.note: #425 established 'read the constant, never transcribe it', and R4 followed it. Three seats then MEASURED the consequence: a row that reads the constant is green for ANY value of it, so all three timer constants could be changed to values that break the round's claims with every row passing. Reading defeats transcription drift and creates blindness to the constant itself. BOTH are needed -- read it, and assert an absolute consequence derived from outside the header. Fixed for diff_timer in cdc4849. EVERY OTHER DIFFERENTIAL IN regress/ HAS THIS SHAPE AND NONE HAS BEEN CHECKED.

AUDITED, and the answer bounds the finding rather than leaving it open. All seven regress/diff_*.c were checked for macros on the EXPECTED side of a row. Four use none at all (diskimage_geom, ieee_store, sh4_tmu, wdc_identify). The two disk differentials use only TYPE TAGS and OPCODES -- DISKIMAGE_SCSI/FLOPPY/IDE, SCSICMD_READ_10, SCSICMD_REQUEST_SENSE, MACHINE_PMAX/EVBMIPS -- and those DO NOT carry the risk: changing such a value is a rename that code and test follow together, with no behaviour to break. The risk is specific to a constant encoding a THRESHOLD or POLICY, where a different value IS different behaviour and the reading row follows it silently. *** diff_timer.c was the ONLY differential exposed, and it is fixed in cdc4849. *** The open-ended worry ('every differential has this shape and none has been checked') is now closed by measurement; what remains is the RULE, which applies to any future differential that reads a tunable.

rows.title: mrwstore2  A straddling store whose tail faults makes an MMIO head see the write twice
rows.hold: not introduced by #430, but newly easier to reach

The differential's E4 comment records the READ side of partial completion honestly; this is the store side, and it is the one with a visible consequence. The memblock split has had this property all along, but the page split fires 256x more often.

rows.title: m8820x  CMMU: any unhandled offset in a 4 KB window exits the host -- ON A BOOTING RIG

closure.note: SHIPPED 66b0367. Nine seats; the measuring seat booted the guest with instrumentation and the adjudicating seat caught that the fix as designed would have introduced a SILENTLY IGNORED TLB FLUSH -- so the seven-command fold ships in the same diff. MEASURED: the reproduction goes 1007 -> 0; 15 rows / 0 failures; census 6 mutants, 6 killed, 0 survived; gate 2 195 checks; luna88k boots VERDICT=PASS with ZERO m8820x complaints, which is the boot census confirmed from the other side; gate_mips 6/6. mvme187 inherits the fix for free.

entries.note: *** THIS OUTRANKS EVERYTHING ELSE QUEUED, AND IT WAS FOUND BY A PARALLEL READ-ONLY SUB-AGENT WHILE #432 WAS BEING IMPLEMENTED. *** dev_m8820x.c:220 has a `default:` arm calling exit(1) on ANY unhandled offset -- READS as well as writes -- and M8820X_LENGTH is 0x1000 (cpu_m88k.h:229), 1024 word offsets, of which the switch handles 21. dev_m8820x is memory-mapped on LUNA88K (dev_luna88k.c:902,:915), which is one of the three rigs that BOOTS IN THIS TREE TODAY -- so unlike footbridge this is reproducible. Four more on the same rig, all CONFIRMED: dev_luna88k.c:816, and dev_m8820x.c:159 (read of CMMU_SCR), :152 (write to the read-only CMMU_IDR), :169 (write to the read-only CMMU_SSR), plus :125 transitively via m8820x_command(). Ruled out while checking: regs[] is sized M8820X_LENGTH/4 so the unconditional read at :145 is in bounds -- no OOB hiding behind the exit. The CMMU_CSSP1/2/3 example is REAL but weaker than first reported: m8820x.h says those 'only exist on 88204'. The 21-of-1024 gap stands regardless. memory_rw.c:572-578 already plumbs the #220 `cpu->running = 0` pattern, so the fix needs no new machinery.

REPRODUCED BEFORE ANY EDIT, and worse than filed. An offline driver drove every word offset in the mapped window through the shipped dev_m8820x_access, each probe forked so one host kill did not end the run: of 1024 word offsets, **1013 READS and 1015 WRITES terminate the host process** -- 99.0% of the window on a plain read -- and only 11 reads survive. The handled-offset count is 18 (case labels listed), not the 21 first filed; the correction STRENGTHENS the finding. Four exit(1) calls sit inside the handler, so the in-arm exits add to the default arm rather than being covered by it.

CAUGHT A DEFECT IN THE REPRODUCTION ITSELF, from the source alone, and predicted the corrected numbers exactly. No bit below 26 can affect any interrupt decision. So store-as-is and store-masked are behaviourally identical for delivery, and 'return without storing' is the ONE option that differs materially -- it leaves the old mask in force while the guest believes its SPL changed. THE ADVERSARIAL FINDING, and it BOUNDS THE ROUND: the settled two-arm doctrine has a MISSING THIRD ARM, and a mechanical sweep would ship a worse defect than it removes.
* sh4_dmac_transfer (dev_sh4.c:340-428, DEVICE_ACCESS-reachable, exits at :372/:381/:390/:422/:427): the ONLY implemented CHCR_RS mode is 0x200, which by its own comment transfers nothing; there is no memory-to-memory path at all. Apply complain-and-continue and a guest programming ordinary dual-address DMA gets NO BYTES MOVED, CHCR_TE never set, no interrupt -- it polls TE forever or reads a destination that was never written. Silent corruption or a silent hang surfacing in a driver far from the DMAC, strictly HARDER to diagnose than today's exit(1), which names the mode in one line.
* AND THE LATCH MAKES IT WORSE, NOT BETTER: for a hot STATUS register latching is right, but for a STATEFUL OPERATION the first dropped transfer reports and every later one is invisible -- the latch actively SUPPRESSES the evidence of accumulating divergence. That inverts the #433 refinement instead of extending it.
* Same class at sh4_pcic's window-base registers (PCIMBR :917, PCIIOBR :926, PCILAR0/1 :891/:909, PCILSR0/1 :882/:900): dropping a write leaves the emulator decoding at the OLD base while the guest believes it moved, so every later PCI access lands at the wrong address -- possibly on a different device that answers.
* NOT A NEW CLASS -- #433's own adjudication hit it once (FLUSH_SUPER_LINE: a silently ignored TLB flush leaves the guest translating through a torn-down mapping) and solved it LOCALLY, without writing the rule down. So a mechanical pass over 170 sites would ship it at least three more times.
* THE ARM, stated so it applies per site: complain-and-continue is safe ONLY when the dropped write's only observable consequence is the register's own value. If the write's PURPOSE is to change how the emulator decodes, translates, transfers or invalidates -- address windows, TLB/cache flushes, DMA descriptors, coherency ops -- dropping it makes the model LIE rather than LAG, and the guest cannot tell. For that class: implement it, or stop honestly with cpu->running = 0 (which unlike exit(1) preserves the debugger and the emulator's own diagnostics) -- NEVER a latched drop. Three meanings, not two.
* AND THE ARM VINDICATES THE ROUND'S OWN SITE RATHER THAN BLOCKING IT: INT_ST_MASK IS state-changing (it is an SPL write), BUT the guarded portion -- bits 25..0 -- is MEASURED DEAD, so store-as-is drops nothing and the latched shape is correct at :816. That is exactly why this one site is safe and a blanket sweep is not.  [panel_20260817_112300]

entries.note: UNBLOCKED: the 21285 datasheet was obtained (_scratchpad/dc21285.pdf, Intel 278115-001). Four defects are now specifiable. (1) SS7.3.41 bit 6: FREERUN wraps to FFFFFFh and keeps counting; PERIODIC reloads TimerNLoad; the clock source is bits 3:2 alone, identical in both. reload_timer_value() computes one rate and hands it to a repeating timer -- the PERIODIC cadence unconditionally -- so a FREERUN timer is too fast by up to 2^24/load. (2) TimerNValue is READ-ONLY (SS7.3.38/7.3.40) but the model accepts a guest write, and TIMER_1_CLEAR has NO writeflag test, so a guest READ of a write-only register reloads the counter and deasserts the IRQ. (3) Reset values diverge: hardware gives CONTROL 0x00 and LOAD 0, the model gives TIMER_MODE_PERIODIC and TIMER_MAX_VAL -- and this is the model bug #432's first draft mistakenly cited as evidence for its own zero mapping. (4) The random() counter model is now fully specified by SS7.3.40 + SS7.3.41 bit 7: a 24-bit down-counter, readable any time, RETAINED across disable and resuming on re-enable. The author's TODO is discharged; only a rig is missing.

Expand the item: external-event handling, reserved CONTROL-bit masking, and the retained/down-counter model belong in it alongside the four already listed. Ordering it after i8253zero would also be defensible, since i8253zero has a direct datasheet answer.

rows.title: i8253zero  A programmed count of 0 means 65536, not 'disabled' -- now datasheet-backed
rows.hold: settled by document; one-line fix in the hz computation

entries.note: SETTLED FROM A REAL DOCUMENT, which is the whole point of the item. i8253reg.h says nothing about a zero count (read in full, 102 lines), so the belief rested on memory -- exactly the trap this project names. The Intel 8254 datasheet (_scratchpad/i8254.pdf, 231164-005) states it twice on p.17: 'The largest possible initial count is 0; this is equivalent to 2^16 for binary counting and 10^4 for BCD counting.' So dev_8253.c:125's `else hz = 0` -- which the timer core then floor-clamps to 1e-8 Hz, i.e. never fires -- is wrong against the hardware convention. Cite it as the 8254, NOT the 8253: the count-0 convention was verified in the 8254 document only.

rows.title: fbpending  footbridge pending_timer_interrupts is an uncapped int, never decremented by the tick
rows.hold: same class as #432, same registers; not a regression

entries.note: From R6 pass 2 (measuring seat, MANUAL). pending_timer_interrupts[] is a plain int, incremented from the SIGALRM handler with NO cap, and DEVICE_TICK never decrements it -- only TIMER_x_CLEAR (by one) and the disable path do. On cats (emulated_hz 50 MHz) a LEGAL load=1 with ENABLE accrues ~5e7/s and reaches signed-int overflow in ~43 s; four timers at the catch-up ceiling do it in ~7.9 s. NOT a regression -- the same was reachable before #432 -- but it is the same class as the bug just fixed, in the same registers, and #432's own text computes the 31 s figure while attributing it to a REJECTED design rather than to the shipped one.

rows.title: m8probe  m8820x PROBE_USER/PROBE_SUPER are dropped, so SSR answers a deterministic miss
rows.hold: no measured guest issues probes; needs the translation walk

entries.note: From R7. After #433 a probe is complained-once and dropped, and the guest then reads regs[CMMU_SSR], which nothing ever writes -- the model writes only PFSR/PFAR (memory_m88k.c:382-405) -- so probes deterministically answer 0, i.e. V-bit clear, a defined 'no valid translation' rather than a plausible-looking valid answer. The measured OpenBSD/luna88k boot issues NO probes (7 command values, all handled); NetBSD and MP kernels are unmeasured. Real semantics mean reusing the existing translation walk against regs[CMMU_SAR] and synthesising SSR from the header's bit definitions (m8820x.h:155-163). No 88200 manual exists in-tree, so where a bit's setting condition is not derivable from the header plus the existing walk, leave it 0 and record UNKNOWN.

entries.note: From R7. dev_m8820x.c's PFSR/PFAR/SAR/SCTR/SAPR/UAPR arm calls invalidate_translation_caches(c, 0, INVALIDATE_ALL) BEFORE the writeflag check, so plain READS purge every translation. PFSR is read on fault paths, so this may fire per-fault for a whole boot. THIS IS ALSO THE MECHANISM THAT CORRUPTED THE FIRST REPRODUCTION -- the offline driver left that callback NULL and six offsets crashed in the harness. Test-first: instrument a counter across a full luna88k boot on a scratch copy; if ~0, close as 'assessed, not changed'. If hot, move the invalidate under the writeflag check -- reads have no architectural invalidation semantics to preserve, and keeping it on writes preserves every existing correctness cue.

REPRODUCED TEST-FIRST, 4 rows / 0 failures, REPRO_M8INVREAD_CONFIRMED. dev_m8820x.c:304-314 groups PFSR, PFAR, SAR, SCTR, SAPR and UAPR and calls invalidate_translation_caches(c, 0, INVALIDATE_ALL) UNCONDITIONALLY, one line ABOVE the `if (writeflag == MEM_WRITE)` that stores -- so each of the six purges the emulator's entire dyntrans mapping on a plain READ. Measured 1 purge per register, 6 of 6, counted through an installed no-op callback rather than inferred. THREE CONTROLS HOLD, and they are what make it a measurement rather than a reading: the WRITE side still purges 6 (deliberately not under test), reading IDR from outside the group purges 0 (so the count is this arm and not something ambient), and the read still returns the seeded value 0xabcd (so a later fix cannot pass by turning the read into a no-op). WHY IT IS NOT MERELY UNTIDY: PFSR and PFAR are what a fault handler READS to find out what faulted and where, so the cost lands on the ordinary page-fault path, twice per fault. Per-boot read count NOT yet measured. THIS IS THE SAME CALLBACK whose NULLness corrupted the first m8820x reproduction by exactly six each way -- that accident was this defect seen from the other side.

*** TRUNCATED TWICE AS A SEAT FAILURE, THEN ANSWERED 10,431 BYTES IN THE FOREGROUND -- a HARNESS defect, not a quota wall. *** Backgrounding panel.sh kills the waiter and at least this seat; the verdict went to stdout only, so the run looked complete. panel.sh now writes $OUT/SEATS.txt plus a PANEL_COMPLETE sentinel. The sharpest restores the read purge under a value guard (`writeflag == MEM_READ && odata != 0`): it passed all 21^H17 rows, passed diff_m8820x.c, BOOTED THE RIG 1:1:1 -- and restores 144,536 of ~286,500 purges, HALF THE DEFECT. rows.title: m8online  Commit the cold-debugger probe: guest-instruction reachability, 3.1 s

closure.note: The detector the offline differential cannot be: it proves REACHABILITY, not just behaviour, and would go red under a change that unmapped the device. Structurally immune to the harness artifact that corrupted this round's first offline reproduction -- a harness fault emits no m8820x diagnostic at all.

entries.note: From R7. The committed differential proves the device's behaviour but NOT that the site is reachable by a guest instruction through the real memory path -- it calls dev_m8820x_access directly, so it cannot catch a change that makes the device unreachable (a memory_device_register length or DM_ flag change). The measuring seat built and measured the alternative: a cold-debugger probe, no boot, 3.1 s for 8 rows, ~60-75x cheaper than a rig drive, with every probe word disassembled before stepping. It is also structurally immune to the harness artifact that fooled the first reproduction: a harness fault produces no m8820x diagnostic at all. Rows must assert VALUES not survival (control r4 == 0x00a90000) and cover ALL FIVE sites, since a fix repairing only the default arm passes any detector that probes 0x800 alone. Do NOT add a booting-rig row: the fix is measured boot-neutral, so such a row could only re-assert what gate_ab already asserts, at ~200 s of load-sensitive wall clock.

SHIPPED. 9 of 9 rows survive a REAL GUEST INSTRUCTION through the real address decode and memory_rw plumbing, where five terminated the host before #433, each printing the complain-once diagnostic with its instance. VALUES NOT SURVIVAL: the first row loads CMMU_IDR and asserts 0x00a90000, the seeded 88200 rev-9 id, which can only have come back through the device. The fold is checked end to end -- command 0x34 survives SILENTLY (handled) while 0x24 still complains once. Every planted word is disassembled and matched before stepping, and the gate asserts zero dis_ok=False. MEASURED 3.6 s for 9 rows on a cold debugger against 182-233 s for a rig drive; no booting-rig row was added because the fix is boot-neutral and such a row could only re-assert gate_ab. Gate 11 PASS at 80 checks.

rows.title: m8latch  One latch covers four kinds, so one IDR write silences the offset diagnostic
rows.hold: behaviour change; filed rather than widened mid-round

entries.note: From R7 pass 2 (MEASURED). dev_m8820x.c has ONE reported_offset flag covering four kinds of unmodelled access: unhandled offset, IDR write, SCR read, SSR write. Measured 1 of 4 kinds reported -- a guest that writes IDR once permanently demotes the diagnostic for every unmodelled OFFSET it later touches, and debug() is silent at default verbosity. The comment claiming 'each kind is reported in full' is corrected in 12ea008; widening the latch to per-kind is a behaviour change and was deliberately NOT done mid-round.

rows.title: m8snprintf  The unhandled-access message is formatted on every access even when latched
rows.hold: measured 27.7 ns/read, 54.7 ns/write on the latched path

entries.note: From R7 pass 2 (MEASURED). The default arm builds its message with snprintf BEFORE consulting the latch, so the cost is paid on every unmodelled access and then discarded. Measured 27.7 ns/read and 54.7 ns/write on the latched path (absolute, not a delta -- the seat's no-message reference loop was optimised away). Trivial to fix by moving the format inside the latch.

rows.hold: a linker difference would look like a regression

On a toolchain without those, the gate row goes RED rather than SKIP -- a linker difference presenting as a regression, which is the phantom-regression class this project already names. Note the sibling diff_sh4_tmu compile in the same gate does NOT use those flags, so the inconsistency is inside one file.

rows.title: ns16550  Guest-writable divisor divides by zero (UB) -- but not in the shipped build
rows.hold: REAL but optimisation-dependent; NOT the top item

entries.note: REPRODUCED TEST-FIRST, AND IT CORRECTS THE FILING AND MY OWN RANKING. Two seats filed this as the cheapest remaining guest-reachable HOST KILL on the live arc rig; I ranked it top of the queue on that. MEASURED: SIGFPE with a core dump at -O0 and -O1, SURVIVES at -O2, -O3 and -Os, and SURVIVES under the tree's own build flags (-fgnu89-inline -O3 -DNDEBUG). At -O2+ gcc exploits the UB and elides the division. So the host does NOT die in the configuration this project builds. Still a defect -- UB on a guest-reachable path, restored by any debug build or compiler change -- but not the cheapest host kill and not top of the queue. THE optrow CLASS ON THE OTHER SIDE OF THE GLASS: optrow was a DETECTOR following the compiler, this is a DEFECT following it, and any severity claim about UB must name the flags it was measured under. The vacuity check mattered twice over: read-back confirmed dlab==1 and divisor==0 at the division with debug() reached, so the negative is not a skipped path; and the first run had ALL THREE probes dying INCLUDING THE CONTROL, because calloc left d->addrmult zero and the access function divides relative_addr by it -- the harness producing SIGFPE for the wrong reason, separated from the defect only by the control row.

CONFIRMED from source independently: the divisor is guest-zeroable via the DLAB low-byte write and the divide sits in argument position of a real varargs debug(), so it executes at every verbosity. Its follow-on hypothesis -- that this shape has other instances -- is now REFUTED by measurement: 24 diagnostic-argument divisions in src/, 22 with constant divisors, and the only other non-constant one (diskimage.c:543) cannot reach zero. So ns16550 is the single live instance of the class, and a gate-6 ratchet keeps that true.

rows.title: m8seg  A SEGMENT flush maps to ALL, and the over-invalidation is guest-visible
rows.hold: Behaviour change, not a records fix; the shipped direction is the SAFE one (under-invalidation is what leaves a stale translation). Filed from the R7 pass-2 grok seat, which attacked its own pass-1 advice.

entries.note: The fold sends CMMU_FLUSH_{USER,SUPER}_SEGMENT to the all=1 arm. Safe direction, but NOT free of guest-visible effect, and the shipped comment claimed it was. A walk writes PG_U (and PG_M on a write) back into the page descriptor IN EMULATED MEMORY; a PATC hit sets those bits only in the PATC copy. So a guest that clears U on a page in segment B, flushes segment A, then touches B observes a U bit a correctly-scoped flush would have left clear. The tighter mapping needs no manual: match the walker's own 4 MB segment size, (sar ^ vaddr) & 0xffc00000. What real silicon does at segment granularity is UNKNOWN -- there is no 88200/88204 manual in this project.

rows.title: m8sarpurge  98% of the CMMU arm's write-side purges are gratuitous; the biggest is CMMU_SAR
rows.hold: A second behaviour change on the write side; #434's claim is the one that was A/B measured. Same one-line shape, worth 2.1x as much.

closure.note: Author self-review disclosed. Closed on: 27-row differential 0 failures; census 15 attempted / 15 killed / 0 survived / 0 faults with every kill naming its row; gate 2 PASS at 213 checks; luna88k 1:1:1 to login: with zero m8820x diagnostics on a binary rebuilt from the FINAL source (the pre-commit gate caught that an earlier boot ran against source predating the last three edits). Both pass-2 seats found surviving mutants and both were actioned.

entries.note: Per boot-to-login: PFSR 292,281 reads / SAR 612,186 writes / UAPR 13,026 writes; PFAR read ZERO times. (1) The read side is 99.999% PFSR, so the design brief's 'twice per fault' was WRONG -- it is once, and that sentence was inferred rather than measured. (2) The write side is 98% SAR, and m88k_translate_v2p never consults SAR -- it reads only SAPR/UAPR (memory_m88k.c:135,137), BATC and PATC. SAR is read at exactly one place, dev_m8820x.c:110, as the address operand of a flush command whose own arm already purges at :187. So a SAR write owes no purge BY EXACTLY #434's ARGUMENT FOR READS. (3) Registers that can really change a translation are 13,033 of 917,504 accesses = 1.4%; 98.6% of this arm's purges are unjustified and #434 removes 32% of them.

REPRODUCED TEST-FIRST and MEASURED ON MY OWN INSTRUMENTED BOOT rather than inheriting the assess-phase numbers. Per boot-to-login: PFSR 320,243 reads / 2 writes, PFAR 0/0, SAR 0 reads / 614,262 writes, SCTR 0/2, SAPR 0/5, UAPR 2/13,112. arm_purges 627,383 equals the sum of the six write counts EXACTLY -- the arithmetic control that the counter counts what it claims. Against the device's other purge sites (SCR 602,780, BATC 12) that is 49.9% of every INVALIDATE_ALL the device issues, so the filing's '98% of the write side' understated it.
CONFIRMED COMPLETE on the consumer table, searching every C and header file under src/ for all six constants. The only seat besides the measure seat to close the question rather than flag it as open.

*** CAUGHT THE DESIGN'S CENTRAL SENTENCE BEING FALSE. *** 'No consumer reads these' is wrong for SAR, which IS read at dev_m8820x.c:110 by m8820x_command(). Demanded three distinct reasons instead of one, which is what shipped. Also flagged that my FILING put SCTR in the translation-changing bucket -- also false, also corrected. And insisted on re-pinning E3/E4/F1/E9 in the same commit: 'a green diff_m8invread after this split is a stale pin, not a pass.' Filed rather than folded at its request: a SAPR/UAPR write does not invalidate the guest's PATC (`m8patc`).

SUPPLIED THE STRONGEST EVIDENCE IN THE ROUND, which I had not articulated: the model ITSELF already relies on 'a PFSR write owes no purge' -- the fault path writes PFSR (memory_m88k.c:382-384, dev_luna88k.c:614) and PFAR (:399-405) DIRECTLY through reg[], with no purge, at ~10^5 per boot, against 2 guest writes per boot through this handler. So the change is not a new assumption, it is an existing one applied consistently. It also gave the three-reasons framing verbatim and asked that the #434 comment block be carried forward adapted rather than deleted.

SHIP-WITH-FIX. Correctly identified that the brief's §2 grep only proves the NAMED-CONSTANT access path and does not rule out indexed walks, memcpy/aliasing, or access through cd.m88k.cmmu[] -- 'the single gap that could install a stale translation'. Packet-fed, so it could not close the gap itself; naming it precisely is what a packet seat is for, and the measure seat closed exactly those four shapes.

SHIP-WITH-FIX, converging with glm independently: the consumer table is right for direct constant-indexed access but four indirect shapes are unruled-out, and until those searches come back empty the fix is gating rather than cosmetic. Disclosed plainly that it executed nothing.

*** VERDICT: HOLD -- AND I FIRST RECORDED THIS AS "BELIEVED safe", WHICH SOFTENED A DISSENT INTO AGREEMENT. *** The owner spotted the cell and asked; re-reading the 8.3 KB answer showed the seat had HELD, not concurred. Correcting it is the point of the rule that a dissent is harvested rather than summarised. ITS OBJECTION WAS A REAL CONTRADICTION IN MY OWN BRIEF, not a misreading: packet §2 said PFSR is 'WRITTEN by the fault path; never read', while packet §3's measured table in the same document reported PFSR reads = 320,243. Both sentences were mine. The resolution is that PFSR is never read BY THE TRANSLATION PATH but is read 320,243 times BY THE GUEST through this handler -- two different senses of 'read' that the brief used the same word for. A packet-fed seat can only see what the packet says, and what the packet said was self-contradictory, so HOLD was the correct verdict on the evidence supplied. It graded honestly throughout: CONFIRMED for the arithmetic (it re-added the six write counts to 627,383 itself), UNKNOWN for consumer-table completeness (naming memcpy, pointer arithmetic, indexed access through cd.m88k.cmmu[] and aliasing -- the same four shapes glm and minimax named, which the measure seat then closed), BELIEVED for the SAR ordering while noting the packet never showed the SCR arm to confirm the purge is unconditional and per-CMMU. That last request was ALSO right: the packet had not shown it.

*** CLOSED THE QUESTION THREE SEATS FLAGGED, AND FOUND THAT THE CHANGE TURNS A GATED DETECTOR RED. *** Consumer table CONFIRMED COMPLETE by a CONSTANT CENSUS plus closure of every indirect shape: no memcpy/memmove/bcopy touches a cmmu struct; no escaping pointer into reg[]; reg[] is exactly M8820X_LENGTH/4 words with relative_addr bounded at registration so the index cannot reach batc[]/patc_*[]; the only code iterating the cmmu[] array touches batc[]/patc_*[] and never reg[]. It then read ALL of m88k_translate_v2p and enumerated its complete input set. THE SAR ORDERING HAZARD IS MOOT -- SAR is not in that input set, so no interleaving can make a translation stale; demonstrated by a 10-seed x 60,000-access two-CPU/three-CMMU interleaving differential showing state-equivalence with the purge delta equal to the removed writes on EVERY seed, and negative-controlled against a store-dropped mutant. It built SEVEN mutants: SIX PASSED the four rows the round first planned, including one silently reintroducing purge-on-READ. And it found diff_m8invread.c fails FOUR rows under this change where my own forward note predicted three.

PASS 2, and almost entirely a records review -- eight defects, every one real. The sharpest: the #434 block still said the write side was 'deliberately UNCHANGED' and this item 'not folded in here'; a claim that dropping the store would zero the guest's PFSR reads (FALSE -- the fault path writes PFSR directly, never through this handler); 'no pointer is ever taken into reg[]' (literally false, two local bases, neither escaping); and A SECOND COPY of the 'F1 is the only row' claim already retracted in the same file's header. It also caught that the E9 gate presence check expected 3 because one alternative ALSO matched E4 -- working by accident, and precisely the title-string dependency its own comment criticised. *** AND IT PREDICTED A SURVIVING MUTANT WITHOUT BEING ABLE TO COMPILE ANYTHING: *** an equality guard on UAPR alone, since F4 repeated only SAPR. Built and run against the row set AS IT WAS: DIFF_M8INVREAD_PASS, prediction CONFIRMED. F4 now covers both area pointers.

entries.note: THE BATTERY RE-PROVES THAT DETECTORS PASS AND NEVER RE-PROVES THEY CAN FAIL. Gate 3 (selftest_mutation) is the only failability control and all seven of its mutants target float_emul.c -- none of the five harnesses R4-R9 added. Those censuses ran ONCE, at round time, never again. Presence checks and identity row counts guard deletion and stale copies, not stub drift -- exactly the class m8invground instantiates. Fix: rename it to what it demonstrates, and add ONE in-battery self-mutant row per new diff harness (the pattern gate 2 already owns for absorb and autodev) so failability is re-proved every run, for a few seconds of battery time.

REPRODUCED TEST-FIRST: stubbed all five differentials so check() never compares, keeping row names, row counts, identity rows, failure counts and verdict tokens -- 118 rows detecting nothing, every gate-2 assertion green. Gate 3 mutates ONE file, src/core/float_emul.c, and names none of the five.

*** QUANTIFIED THE WORRY I ASKED IT TO ATTACK, RATHER THAN REASSURING ME. *** It stubbed every row EXCEPT the ones each mutant kills: gate 2 AND the proposed self-mutant both stayed GREEN with 23 of 24 rows inert (timer) and 25 of 27 (m8invread). So the control licenses '1 of 24 rows still detects', not 'the detector is fine' -- MY WORRY WAS CORRECT AS STATED, but it is a NAMING problem: going 0 -> 1 is not false comfort, calling 1 'the detector works' is. It then found the gap is TEN differentials not five, gave a nearly-free in-detector comparator self-check covering all 118 rows at once, PROVED the two controls are complementary (the self-check is blind to a row rewritten to compare the subject against itself; a pinned mutant is not), and measured TWO ways to defeat the control: asserting 'PASS absent' instead of 'FAIL present' (a build failure emits neither, so the negative form is satisfied by a control that never ran) and verdict-only assertion, which is VACUOUS ON 4 OF 5. It built and ran all five mutants, verified each three ways, and independently confirmed the memory_rw floor drift by DELETING six rows and getting 13/13 green. It also disclosed that its own first floor probe was wrong and discarded it.

SUFFICIENT for failability, INSUFFICIENT for row-level correctness -- and it drew the distinction cleanly: the battery's job is detecting regressions, the self-test gate's job is failability meta-testing. Named the false-comfort risk in the same terms Opus later measured.

Converged independently on almost the same implementation spec as the measure seat: gate 2 not gate 3, absorb-shaped applier with count==1, require the named FAIL row AND the DIFF_*_FAIL token, treat crash / empty log / BUILDFAIL as SETUP_FAIL, bump memory_rw 17->23 in the same edit, narrow the gate-3 sentence. Its explicit DO-NOTs matched the two defeats Opus measured. It also insisted the five sibling differentials be FILED not swallowed: 'doing them silently violates the stopping rule; ignoring them after writing the helper repeats the grep-for-siblings miss.' Filed as selfmutant6.

Worked the substitution mechanism in detail and reached the same conclusion the measure seat did: the detectors reach their subject by a QUOTED RELATIVE include, so no -I redirection can point them at a mutant -- the mutant tree must contain the detector too. Proposed mirroring src/ wholesale; the shipped helper symlinks everything and writes one real file, which is the cheaper form of the same idea.

SHIP-WITH-FIX. Correctly identified that the control must be hardened against its own vacuity paths and that the gate assignment needed deciding rather than assuming. Packet-fed, so it could not test either -- naming both precisely is what a packet seat is for.

SHIP-WITH-FIX: one mutant is a necessary smoke test but not a full census; place it in gate 2 beside each harness and FRAME IT AS A FAILABILITY CONTROL, NOT A COVERAGE CLAIM. That framing is what shipped. *** THIS SEAT'S THREE-SEAT GROUP FAILED FIRST WITH ConnectionRefused: the local Ollama server was not running, which produced three 155-byte error files that look exactly like three dead seats. Server restarted, seats re-fired, health-tested live (3.2 s, exact liveness token). panel.sh now PREFLIGHTS the endpoint so one dead server can never again masquerade as three seat failures. ***

SHIP-WITH-FIX and the ONLY DISSENT ON PLACEMENT: it wanted the controls in gate 3 beside the existing float_emul pattern. Overruled BY MEASUREMENT, not by vote -- gate 3 gate_skips on a missing configured tree with config.h and float_emul.h, preconditions these five detectors do not have, so hosting them there would turn 'no build tree' into a SILENT SKIP of the entire failability control. Its other four asks (name a mutant per harness tied to a row identifier, harden against self-vacuity, restate scope as a liveness sentinel) all shipped.

*** 1.9 MB, AND BOTH NEW GATES CAUGHT ME FORGETTING TO RECORD IT -- independently, within a minute of each other: section H saw the stage at 8/9, section G saw the file unread. Neither was contrived; I simply left it out of the ledger write. *** CONFIRMED the stub defeats the whole guard stack, citing the exact line in each of the five where check() is the SOLE writer of `fails`, and noting the identity assertion passes through that same comparator. CONFIRMED no configuration in the sixteen-gate battery catches it, and that -Werror would not help because a stub can retain its parameter uses. Independently CONFIRMED the memory_rw floor drift (17 vs 23) and said to fix it regardless of the sentinel work. Its contract for the control matches what shipped almost clause for clause -- production flags, exactly one DIFF_*_FAIL and zero DIFF_*_PASS, the intended FAIL row, mutant row count equal to the shipped run's. AND IT NAMED A DEFECT THE NEW CONTROLS MUST NOT COPY: gate 3's build_and_run() ignores the mutant's exit status and merely counts DIFF_PASS, so a crash, timeout or empty output scores as DETECTED. Checked: that is ALREADY FILED as (#55). selfmutant.py does not inherit it -- a build failure is scored SETUP, never a detection, and the assertion is that the FAIL token is PRESENT rather than that PASS is absent.

*** FOUR DEFEATS IN THE CONTROLS THE ROUND ITSELF ADDED, all measured, and it disclosed that it had helped shape the design on pass 1 and to discount its agreement accordingly. *** F1: deleting the SELFCHECK block from all five detectors left gate 2 at PASS with the SAME check count and ZERO red rows -- unprotected PRECISELY BECAUSE the bookkeeping is correct, since restoring `rows` is what makes the row invisible to the only mechanism that notices a deletion. F2: the round's two new controls INTERFERED -- the sentinel's healthy-path FAIL lines satisfied the self-mutant's kill pin, so a rowid as ordinary as 'fail' returned SELFMUTANT_OK for a mutant nothing caught, re-opening a defeat the same commit claimed to close. F3: the manifest verified the LEDGER not the WORK -- delete a call and leave the name, or promote a stem and retune the count, both GREEN, with the gate printing the paper shrink as evidence. F4: the sentinel fed alphabetic strings while every real row compares numbers, so one `isdigit` line left 118 rows inert with the sentinel blind and 4 of 5 self-mutants green. It also supplied THE DENOMINATOR THE RECORDS OMITTED -- 148 rows across five differentials remain in exactly the pre-#436 condition, demonstrated by stubbing two of them for 82 inert rows with the battery green, so the round fixed 118 of 266 coverable rows, under half. Three records numbers corrected, including that 'every assertion greps the detector's own stdout' was written in the PRESENT tense by the very hunk that falsified it.

*** FAILED FIRST BY RUNNING A GATE ITSELF -- and the failure was the most useful of the pass. *** It backgrounded gate_offline.sh and printed 'I am waiting for gate_offline.sh to complete' eleven times until its own timeout killed it at 657 bytes. Worse than the lost seat: IT RAN CONCURRENTLY WITH MY OWN GATE 2 IN THE SAME $LOGDIR, so the 'PASS (222 checks)' I had already committed was read from a directory another process was writing. Re-run alone it was identical, so the claim held BY LUCK RATHER THAN PROCESS. panel.sh now appends a no-gates rule to a DERIVED copy of every brief (the caller's file untouched, the derived copy kept beside the answers). Re-fired with that rule it returned 11.6 KB and disclosed its compliance. THEN IT FOUND THREE DEFECTS NO OTHER SEAT DID: two of the five shipped row-id pins were WRONG -- footbridge's 'zero' does not appear in A1 at all (the digit, not the word) and matched B2, E3 and F1, so that mutant vouched for rows it was never chosen for; memory_rw's '1 KB' matched FOUR rows. The anchor-uniqueness trap on the other side of the fence, now closed by requiring a row id to name exactly ONE row. The pristine arm never checked the named row was GREEN, so a decoy FAIL line would satisfy the pin without the mutant doing anything. And the helper compiled memory_rw WITHOUT -fno-optimize-sibling-calls, which this gate calls load-bearing -- a lane divergence the pristine control arm structurally cannot catch, because both arms are then consistently wrong.

NINTH SEAT, VOTES CLOSE. Badge `s` disclosed unprompted: same model as the main loop, so where it merely confirms the main loop's records that is same-model replication, not two-family. Its measurements were run independently in its own WSL copy.
* Q1 THE CORE CLAIM IS HONEST AT THE GRANULARITY IT CLAIMS, with two footnotes it should carry: the claim's universe is gate 2's OFFLINE differentials -- gates 4-16's probe detectors and the ~37 wall-clock oracles still never re-prove failability, which is the next gate3scope-shaped filing and much costlier; and the ONE exemption, ieee_store, rests on gate 3, which asserts the PASS-absent form and carries unfixed #55, so THE 2099 DATE ENTRENCHES THE WEAKEST CONTROL ON THE LARGEST DIFFERENTIAL when a gate-2 selfmutant_one for it would cost minutes.
* Q3 THE HELPER IS NOT AIRTIGHT -- A FOURTH FAILURE MODE, MEASURED. *** M3, THE HANG: build_and_run()'s subprocess.run has NO TIMEOUT. *** A mutant that loops forever (it built one: `for (;;)` inside sh4_timer_tick) makes the helper print NO SELFMUTANT_* TOKEN AT ALL -- not OK, not FAIL, not SETUP -- and wedges gate 2, which the dead-man switch later reports as 'battery NEVER RAN', unattributed. #55's own filed taxonomy was crash/timeout/empty; selfmutant.py closed crash (F5) and empty output (the FAIL-present form) and left TIMEOUT WITH NO ARM WHATSOEVER. For a timer differential 'tick stops advancing' is the most natural regression shape there is.
* Q3 M4, THE NOT-LANDED CLASS, and it UNIFIES the three recorded extra-flags hazards as instances of ONE MISSING POSTCONDITION: the helper never verifies the mutation is present in the tree it compiled. A subject outside the mirrored src/ passes the anchor check, lands in NEITHER arm, and the helper prints 'mutant applied but the detector did NOT report a failure' -- both halves false. One assertion closes the whole class.
* Q2 A THIRD WAY THE MANIFEST IS SATISFIED BY NOTHING, MEASURED by replicating the expiry loop: an exemption whose date is ABSENT or MALFORMED never expires, silently. `ieee_store` with the date typo'd away -> ${_e##*:} returns the whole string, the empty-case arm never fires, string compare is false -> never expires AND still satisfies coverage. `2026-8-1` (unpadded, 18 days past) -> not expired, because '8' > '0'. One regex line closes it.
* MEASURED EN ROUTE: the lane is HERMETIC BY ACCIDENT. misc.h:46's `#include "../../config.h"` escapes the symlinked src/include THROUGH THE SYMLINK'S PARENT back into the real repo root. Benign for every current subject, but 'the lane compiles what the battery compiles apart from the single edit' is true today by include-graph accident rather than by construction.
* Q4 THE QUEUE'S PREMISE IS OFF BY ONE: ELEVEN differentials have a gate-2 self-mutant, not twelve -- ieee_store has gate 3's weak form. The self-mutant DOES subsume total comparator death, so the original 118-row catastrophe is caught wherever a control exists; what the sentinel adds is PARTIAL comparator death on rows the named row does not exercise. Real but second-order. Extend it mechanically and, the load-bearing half, fold the hardcoded 5-list into the manifest idiom -- it is byte-for-byte the F3 defect one control over.
* AND A WRONG RECORD 30 MINUTES OLD, MINE: gate_offline.sh's new comment said 'Floor raised 16 -> 17 with the UNIE-clear row' while its own hunk writes check_min 18 -- a number matching NEITHER the old nor the new value. Corrected in this commit.

But NONE OF THE LADDER'S FOUR RUNGS FIT: they all assume the closed row is an EMULATOR defect with a guest-reachable path, and this round's subject is the TEST APPARATUS itself. `none` would be false because code shipped; `probe:` would be laundering because there is no guest instruction to run.

* *** THE PROPOSED ANTI-LAUNDERING CLAUSE REJECTS THE PROJECT'S OWN EXEMPLAR. *** regress/m8820x_sites_probe.py states the panel's governing principle VERBATIM and is where the principle comes from -- yet it shipped as 9494c6a, THREE COMMITS AFTER the #433 fix 66b0367 (verified), with every row SURVIVED, post-fix only. The principle was lifted out of a DETECTOR and is being written as a rule for WITNESSES.

Where the project conflates them is not in its ENGINEERING but in its RECORDS: round prose says 'reproduced' without naming the artefact.

BUILT AND CLOSED, and it IMPROVED ON THE RECIPE IT WAS GIVEN. Told to build the single-overlay row a prior pass had specified, it built that, then probed two SIBLING mutants and measured that the single-overlay row catches ONLY the deletion: `continue` -> `break;` and `continue` -> `return 0;` both pass it GREEN, because with one overlay there is no next iteration and all three mutants trace identically. A SECOND OVERLAY separates them and one row kills all three. It supplied both patches and recommended the stronger, which also perturbs no existing gate check where the fallback would have forced one from "1" to "2".
* Mechanism: __wrap_fsync consults a static fail_fsync_fd, sets errno=EIO and returns -1 without calling __real_fsync; armed after the WRITE, disarmed when the command returns. It rejected, with reasons written into the file, a real failing fsync (needs dm-error/root, non-portable -- same class as the drvfs trap), close()ing the fd under the live FILE* (a FAULT, and can hit a recycled fd) and an O_RDONLY fd (rc 0 on glibc, proves nothing).
* A CRASH IS NOT WHAT MAKES IT FAIL, measured four ways: rc is 1 never >=128; the mutant printed all 11 rows plus the verdict line so it reached the end of main; ASan+UBSan produced 0 bytes on both arms; and exactly one row differs, by a printed string.

Only a context printout of the line about to be mutated caught it. Correctly anchored on the unique 'Data is not durable' comment: ALL THREE MUTANTS KILLED, traces distinguishable -- deleted publishes b0 anyway, break/return0 stop at F(d0) S(d0).

rows.title: idesync  IDE FLUSH CACHE has no durability path at all -- #437 is SCSI-only

entries.note: grep -i flush src/devices/dev_wdc.c returns NOTHING, so a guest's ATA FLUSH CACHE is not merely unflushed but unimplemented. Reachability UNKNOWN; landisk is the ATA rig and it boots, so a probe witness is likely available.  [panel_20260818_095322]

*** THE BRIEF'S FRAMING WAS HALF WRONG, AND THE HALF IT GOT WRONG CHANGES WHAT SHOULD BE FIXED. *** Verdict FIX-not-document, but not for the reason I gave it.
* 0xE7 WDCC_FLUSHCACHE is DEFINED at wdcreg.h:130 and NEVER REFERENCED in dev_wdc.c; 0xEA has no constant anywhere in src/. Both fall to wdc_command()'s default:, which sets WDCE_ABRT, emits an UNLATCHED fatal(), and -- the part that matters -- does NOT set d->int_assert. MEASURED offline against the shipping wdc_command(): 0xE7 -> err=0x04 irq=0 fatal=1, status 0x51 (DRDY|DSC|ERR), against the 0x10 RECAL control at err=0x00 irq=1.
* NO REAL GUEST ISSUES IT, and the negative is WELL CONTROLLED. With an IDE disk attached and a full filesystem lifecycle (MAKEDEV, fdisk, disklabel, newfs 64 MB FFS, mount, write, sync, umount, halt -p) OpenBSD 7.6 issues exactly: 0xEC 0xF5 0x10 0x91 0xC6 0x20 0xC4 0x30 0xC5 0xE0. No 0xE7, no 0xEA.
* IT REFUTED ITS OWN LEADING HYPOTHESIS rather than resting on it: 'the drive does not advertise FLUSH CACHE' was tested with TWO discriminating IDENTIFY variants (word 83=0x5000 and 0x7000). The guest DEMONSTRABLY READ the new IDENTIFY -- it began issuing 0xEF SET FEATURES, which it never did before -- and STILL never flushed. Why OpenBSD declines is an honest UNKNOWN: there is no OpenBSD source in this tree, and reconstructing wd_flushcache from memory is exactly the trap the SH-manual rule exists to prevent.
* *** THE LIVE DEFECT IS THE ARM, NOT THE OPCODE: 0xE0 STANDBY IMMEDIATE hits the same default: on EVERY `halt -p`, measured 4 of 4 shutdown runs. *** ABRT to the guest, no interrupt, unlatched host warning, and the guest swallows it silently. So the IDE side has a reachable reproducible fall-through TODAY, and FLUSH CACHE is an unreached member of the same set.
* THE FIX IS NOT A ONE-LINER. diskimage_sync() takes a struct diskimage *, but dev_wdc.c only ever holds (machine, id, type) -- and THERE IS NO EXPORTED (machine,id,type) -> struct lookup; every public function in diskimage.c open-codes the same 6-line walk. Needs a diskimage_sync_id() wrapper, a WDCC_FLUSHCACHE_EXT constant, and a case arm that also sets int_assert. Built privately: 0xE7/0xEA become err=0x00 irq=1 fatal=0 with trace F(data) S(data), matching the SCSI sibling.
* DETECTOR BUILT, and it COMPILES AGAINST BOTH TREES because the rows pass a RAW OPCODE INTEGER rather than the WDCC_ constant -- deliberately sidestepping the exact trap diff_diskimage_sync.c's header records, where naming the new symbol made the pre-fix arm a SETUP result. 9 rows / 0 failed pre-fix; 8 of 9 flip post-fix. Needs only two extra stubs given the flags gate_offline.sh already passes.
* SCOPE: all three files are byte-identical between est/ and GXEMUL-SEC/. And wdc is far from landisk-only -- bus_isa, bus_pci, dev_pcic, dev_ps2_spd, machine_arc.c:235, machine_landisk.c:87 and promemul/of.c all instantiate it, so ARC IS A SECOND ATA RIG THAT WAS NOT TESTED.  [agent idesync 2026-08-19]

The item: #429 range-checks a guest rate inside dev_rtc.c, and the filing argued the narrowing should move into the timer core instead, where every device that derives a rate from a guest value would get it. *** THE PREMISE IS STALE AND TWO SEATS MEASURED IT INDEPENDENTLY. *** The filing named dev_footbridge, dev_vr41xx and dev_jazz as unguarded. Read today: dev_jazz.c:432-434 computes 1000.0/(idata+1.0), bounded above by 1000 and bounded BY CONSTRUCTION since b679170 (#257, 2026-07-18); dev_vr41xx.c:604-612 is `int hz = RTCL1_L_HZ / idata` with RTCL1_L_HZ = 0x8000 (vr_rtcreg.h:90), an unsigned divide so hz <= 32768; dev_footbridge derives from emulated_hz over a 32-bit divisor and its +INF path is already fixed. NONE of the three can exceed TIMER_MAX_FREQUENCY. So the wide-domain narrowing case that justified a four-device round does not exist. What IS shared is the OPPOSITE END: all three can land below TIMER_MIN_FREQUENCY, which timer_clamp_freq floors SILENTLY -- timer.c:100-108 sets was_clamped only on the ceiling.
